slides.say: In the accompanying figure, lines a and b are both perpendicular to line c. Line d crosses lines a and b. What is the value of x?

x is at line b, and the only number we have, fifty degrees, is at line a. To move an angle from one line to the other, the two lines must be parallel. But the question doesn't say that a is parallel to b. [short pause] So first we'll check if we can prove it.
[short pause] Look at line c. Line a is perpendicular to it, and line b is perpendicular to it too. The little squares show that.

Two lines that are perpendicular to the same line are parallel. They both go straight across, in the same direction, so they never meet. So a is parallel to b, even though the question doesn't write it.
at: Two lines that are perpendicular to the same line
So a is parallel to b

slides.say: Now we don't need line c anymore. It's the usual picture: two parallel lines, a and b, and line d that cuts them.
at: we don't need line c anymore

slides.say: The fifty degrees at line a is one of the small angles. All the small angles are equal, so the small angle at line b, above b and to the right of d, is fifty degrees too.
at: The fifty degrees at line a
so the small angle at line b

slides.say: x is right next to that fifty, on the other side of line d. Together they make the straight line b, so fifty plus x is a hundred eighty.
at: x is right next to that fifty

slides.say: x is a hundred eighty minus fifty, which is a hundred thirty. Choice number three is our answer.
at: x is a hundred eighty minus fifty
Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: Careful with choice number four. It's true that the question doesn't write that a is parallel to b, but the two right angles prove it, so x can be found. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
